Rooms.Name: End of the trail
Rooms.Description:
The trail through the forest ends rather abruptly, blocked by a rocky 
outcrop, covered with thick bushes. It seems odd for such an obviously 
well trodden path to end this way, and the more you look at it the more 
odd it seems. The trail disappears under the bushes, perhaps you should 
take a closer look at them.

Exits.Description: A narrow trail winds its way through the forest.
The trail disappears beneath some bushes.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The trail goes right up to and under the bushes. You think you can see 
an opening beneath them.

Rooms.Name: Tunnel
Rooms.Description:
You find yourself in a narrow tunnel leading east. The walls are 
fairly obviously not naturally formed, but crafted from the rocks by 
hand.  The tunnel is faintly lit by phosphorescent rocks, that give off 
a dull green glow making your hands look like those of a monster.

Exits.Description: The tunnel continues to the east.
You can see daylight above, obstructed by bushes.

Rooms.Name: End of the tunnel
Rooms.Description:
The tunnel ends before a magnificent carving in the rock. Carved upon 
the smooth rock face, it is a circular pattern, covered in stars and 
astronomical symbols.  You notice that the centre of the carving is the 
moon.  The carving is inlaid with some dark metal that shimmers in the 
dim light from the rocks.

Exits.Description: A huge and intricate carving covers the south wall.
The tunnel continues to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The centre of the carving is a full moon, the intricate carvings that 
surround it are amazing in their detail. Astrological symbols feature 
quite heavily, but in addition to the familiar constellations are five 
carvings of forest creatures - a vicious tiger, a rampaging boar, a 
ferocious wolf, a stealthy cat and a sneaky looking rat. A careful study 
reveals that the carving is cunningly hinged.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to Werehome
Rooms.Description:
You are at the entrance to a huge underground complex, carved out of 
the mountain.  Streets lead off in all directions and people walk about 
minding their own business.  The streets are lit by more of the strange 
glowing rocks, but unlike the tunnel, the streets are as bright as 
daylight.

Exits.Description: You can see the rear of a huge carved door.
A dark pathway leads east.
The main street continues to the south.
An avenue lined with stately homes can be found to the west.

Rooms.Name: Avenue of the Tigers
Rooms.Description:
This part of town is populated by the ruling class of werehome - the
Tigers. The houses along this street are beautifully decorated, the 
gardens well kept.  The Avenue of Tigers continues to the west, and to 
the north and south you can see some of their homes.

Exits.Description: A Weretiger estate can be seen to the north.
You see the entrance to Werehome.
A Weretiger estate can be seen to the south.
The avenue continues to the west.

Rooms.Name: Avenue of the Tigers
Rooms.Description:
More estates lie to the north and south of this end of the Avenue. To
the west a large square can be seen. Although the tigers are a class 
above the rest, they seem to all mix freely in the streets, you can see 
cunning rat folk talking to stealthy cats, strutting boars and powerful 
wolves.

Exits.Description: A Weretiger estate can be seen to the north.
The avenue continues to the east.
A Weretiger estate can be seen to the south.
You can make out a beautiful fountain in the distance.

Rooms.Name: Fountain Square
Rooms.Description:
The avenue of the Tigers ends in a large square, dominated by a large
fountain, which spills clear water out into a wide basin. Benches 
surround the fountain, where small groups of werefolk sit, enjoying the 
peace and quiet of this area of town. There are small alcoves to the 
north and west, and to the south you can see several large, and busy 
temples.

Exits.Description: You see glittering multicoloured lights.
The Avenue of the Tigers leads east.
Temple Street lies to the south.
You see a shop full of adventuring equipment.

Rooms.Name: Tiger's Estate
Rooms.Description:
The Tigers are considered to be the most civilised, and most 
human-like of the werefolk, and their homes seem to emulate the 
dwellings of richer humans. Beautiful gardens surround the main 
house, which is well constructed and decorated with pink marble, 
and black granite cladding. You feel it would be rude to wander in 
and look around without permission.

Exits.Description: The Avenue of the Tigers lies to the south.

Rooms.Name: Tiger's Estate
Rooms.Description:
All the Tigers estates seem to be different, they apparently take 
pride in their individuality, and love to show off their good taste and 
hospitality. This particular house has a water garden, with miniature 
rivers and lakes, filled with tiny fish. Its pretty impressive - the 
kind of thing you would expect to see among the wealthier humans. 
Although you still feel it would be rude to wander round the house 
uninvited, the owners could hardly mind you taking a look round the 
gardens.

Exits.Description: You can see a beautiful water garden.
The Avenue of the Tigers lies to the south.

Rooms.Name: The water garden
Rooms.Description:
You are following a narrow gravel pathway round the back of one of 
the Tigers' houses. Lovely willow trees shade you from the artificial 
light shining down on you from above. A couple of golden carp are 
feeding in the narrow waterway on one side of the path, which crosses a 
little hump-back bridge to a serene looking glade, complete with gazebo.

Exits.Description: The rest of the estate is to the south.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
If you don't know what a gazebo is, then you are clearly far too 
uncultured for this place, you'd better leave before someone starts 
asking questions.

Rooms.Name: Tiger's Estate
Rooms.Description:
The front of this estate is dominated by glorious marble columns, 
decorated with fanciful scrollwork. Sweeping pathways circle the garden, 
which is filled with bushes which have been carefully trimmed into the 
shape of birds. Strangely, considering there is no natural sunlight, a 
sundial is also here. Clearly this is just another fashion accessory for 
the well cultured weretiger.

Exits.Description: The Avenue of the Tigers lies to the north.

Rooms.Name: Tiger's Estate
Rooms.Description:
This particular estate has the look of the orient about it. You guess
that oriental fashions must be the latest to take the fancy of the 
cosmopolitan weretigers, the paint work is hardly dry and there is 
evidence of the recent construction work.

Exits.Description: The Avenue of the Tigers lies to the south.

Rooms.Name: The Loremaster's Cave
Rooms.Description:
The Loremaster is the most ancient and learned of the werefolk. He 
lives a fairly solitary life, although he is often visited by people who 
wish to benefit from his wisdom. The strange crystals that light 
werehome are multicoloured here, making the cave look like the inside 
of some fantastic gem.

Exits.Description: You can see the fountain square.

Rooms.Name: The Expedition Shop
Rooms.Description:
A knowledgeable looking werewolf sells useful items to any aspiring 
adventurers. All expeditions outside werehome have to be sanctioned by 
the House of Lords, with the exception of werewolves who can come and 
go as they please. Aaron the shopkeeper makes sure they are properly 
equipped.

Exits.Description: You can see the fountain square.

Rooms.Name: Lower Temple Street
Rooms.Description:
The werefolk come to this quarter of town to worship their totems. 
There are five temples in town, the rats and cats have their places of 
worship at the lower end of temple street, the boar and wolf temples are 
located on upper temple street to the south, near to the temple of the 
tigers.

Exits.Description: You can see the fountain square.
Werecats are entering and leaving the building to the east.
Temple Street continues to the south.
Wererats are scurrying in and out of the temple to the west.

Rooms.Name: Temple of the Rat
Rooms.Description:
The inside of the temple of the Rat is laid out in a circular pattern
around a statue of the vicious looking wererat. It appears that the 
wererats prefer to worship in their humanoid form, beautiful woven rugs 
cover the floor, and there is an offering tray next to the door. There 
is a small doorway leading south, which you assume leads to the priests' 
quarters.

Exits.Description: The bright light of temple street beckons you outside.

Tattered banners, and ugly statues cover the south wall, apart from 
where it is interrupted by a small door.

Rooms.Name: Inner sanctum of the Rat Temple
Rooms.Description:
The inner sanctum is where the clergy of the wererats meet and 
perform their most sacred rites. The room is filled with what you would 
describe as junk, but what probably constitutes the wererat's most holy 
relics. A wererats first metamorphosis takes place here, under the 
supervision of the priests.

Exits.Description: The main chamber of the rat temple lies to the north.

Rooms.Name: Temple of the Cat
Rooms.Description:
The temple of the cat has a large domed ceiling, painted with large 
numbers of werecats in various phases of transformation. A white marble 
altar, carved with feline symbols stands at the focus of several tiers 
of seats arranged in an arc.

Exits.Description: There is a small door in the middle of the east wall.
You can see the bustle of Temple Street.

Rooms.Name: Sanctum of the cat temple
Rooms.Description:
The inner sanctum of the werecats is given over to peaceful 
meditation. The lighting is provided by pleasantly scented candles, 
which surround the room. There are cushions everywhere, and werecats 
sleeping on some of them. It seems that meditation to the werecats 
consists of spending a great deal of time asleep. Some of them have even 
taken on their animal form, in order to better get in touch with their 
inner selves.

Exits.Description: The main part of the temple lies to the west.

Rooms.Name: Upper Temple Street
Rooms.Description:
You are reaching the classier end of the temple quarter, where the 
upper echelons of were-society come to worship their totems. To the 
south stands the incredible temple of the tiger,  and to the west is the 
temple of the boar. Dark steps lead upwards to the temple of the wolf, 
which is by far the busiest temple you have seen.

Exits.Description: Lower Temple Street lies to the north.
An alley leads east, an quickly opens out into a large square.
You see a magnificent temple, with weretigers wandering in and out.
Wereboars are wandering in and out of the temple to the west.
Black granite steps lead up to the Temple of the Wolf.

Rooms.Name: Temple of the Boar
Rooms.Description:
The temple of the Boar is remarkably similar in layout to the temple 
of the Tiger. You realise that more than anything else the boars would 
like the respect that the tigers have. Unfortunately the similarity just 
makes the temple of the boar look rather cheap - a poor imitation of a 
better original. Statues line the walls, and a granite altar, covered 
with a rich purple altar cloth stands in the centre of the temple.

Exits.Description: You can see the busy Upper Temple Street to the east.
A careful search indicates that the altar can be moved.

Rooms.Name: Sanctum of the Boar
Rooms.Description:
The boars might want to emulate the noble tigers, but that doesn't 
mean that they aren't dedicated to worshipping their boar totems. The 
inner sanctum is decorated with statues of their ancestors, some of them 
in humanoid form, and some taking the form of a mighty boar.

Exits.Description: Steps lead up to the Temple of the Boar.

Rooms.Name: Temple of the Wolf
Rooms.Description:
The oldest and most powerful sect of the werecreatures, the wolves 
have a rich history and a central role in the city. While the Tigers 
rule, it is the wolves that are the warriors, the hunters and the most 
feared of the werefolk. Its generally accepted that the tigers rule, 
because the wolves have better things to do with their time, and one of 
those things is here in this temple. All the wolves can shapeshift from 
humanoid to wolf form, seemingly at will and without effort and it is 
this talent that sets them apart from the other werecreatures.

Exits.Description: A black door, carved with a wolfshead, leads south.
Black granite steps lead down to Upper Temple Street.

Rooms.Name: Temple of the Tiger
Rooms.Description:
The tigers take their religion very seriously, but it is not the 
same as the devotion of the wolves, more likely it is fashionable to be 
pious and so the temple is the place to be seen. The temple itself looks 
vaguely familiar and it takes you a while to realise that it is based 
on the temple of Midgaard, which of course was the height of fashion 
when it was constructed many centuries ago. The altar lies to the west, 
and behind it is a monstrous statue of a tiger, walking upright on his 
hind feet.

Exits.Description: You can see the busy Upper Temple Street to the north.

The Temple of the Tiger extends further to the west, where you can see 
the altar and a huge statue.

Rooms.Name: Behind the Altar
Rooms.Description:
The statue towers fifty feet above you, all carved from pristine 
white marble and depicting a ferocious tiger standing on his hind feet. 
You have to admit, its pretty impressive. The altar stands as high as 
your shoulder, and is carved with astrological symbols.

Exits.Description: You can see the main part of the temple.
There is a small trapdoor behind the statue.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The statue is hauntingly realistic, with eyes like thunder and razor 
sharp claws. As you look around the back of it you notice a small 
trapdoor set into the base.

Rooms.Name: Main Street
Rooms.Description:
You stand at a junction along the main street in werehome. The 
street continues south towards an official looking building, which you 
assume is some kind of government centre. There are streets to the east 
and west, which seem to lead to housing areas.

Exits.Description: The main street continues to the north.
A wide street leads east.
To the south you can see a huge, very official looking building.

The alley to the east is very narrow, and dimly lit. Something smells 
peculiar down this path.

Rooms.Name: Ghetto of the Rat-people
Rooms.Description:
The homes of the wererats are untidy and disorganised. To your 
civilised eyes, this area appears nothing more than a ghetto. Cluttered 
streets run in all directions, though most of them look impassable. The 
houses look as if they would collapse under a stiff breeze, and a much 
needed breeze it would be too, this place stinks!

Exits.Description: You can see a winding muddy alley to the north.
The main street lies to the east.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the south.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the west.

Rooms.Name: In the ghetto
Rooms.Description:
Tiny streets run in all directions, though only the north and south 
pathways look passable in safety. The eyes of the inhabitants watch you 
suspiciously from the hovel-like dwellings. The inhabitants don't seem to 
notice the smell, or the precarious situation of the housing.

Exits.Description: You can see a winding muddy alley to the north.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the east.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the south.

Rooms.Name: In the ghetto
Rooms.Description:
You are surrounded by bad housing and unnatural smells. (Probably 
best not to try and imagine what is causing those smells.) The houses 
lean dangerously over the streets, which look passable only to the north 
and east.

Exits.Description: You can see a winding muddy alley to the north.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the east.

Rooms.Name: In the ghetto
Rooms.Description:
The muddy twisty streets are becoming confusing, you can't seem to 
remember which way you came. There is a pile of junk against the wall of 
one of the houses here, it seems the rats are great scavengers, but its 
unlikely you'll find anything valuable in there, more likely you will 
catch some disease.

Exits.Description: You can see a winding muddy alley to the east.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the south.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the west.
Junk covers a set of steps leading down.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Rummaging around in the junk you find a narrow stepladder leading down.

Rooms.Name: In the ghetto
Rooms.Description:
You are surrounded by bad housing and unnatural smells. (Probably 
best not to try and imagine what is causing those smells.) The houses 
lead dangerously over the streets, which look passable only to the north, 
west and east.

Exits.Description: You can see a winding muddy alley to the north.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the east.
You can see a winding muddy alley to the west.

Rooms.Name: Before the Lords
Rooms.Description:
The Werehome House of Lords is where all the important decisions 
are made, and the building itself looks important too. The front is 
supported by large fluted columns, in fact the whole building looks 
very much like a roman basilica. A narrow, but well trodden pathway 
leads to the east, you see wolves heading down there and assume that 
is where they live. To the west you can make out the busy Upper 
Temple Street.

Exits.Description: The main street continues to the north.
You can see wolves wandering down this pathway.
You can enter the House of Lords
You can see the crowds gathering at Upper Temple Street.

Rooms.Name: House of Lords
Rooms.Description:
There are Lords among all races of werefolk, and despite the social 
standing of the different types, all have equal standing before the law 
of Werehome. Permission is required by anyone wanting to leave 
Werehome and go above ground, and it is here they must petition the 
Lords to gain permission. The only exceptions to the rule are the 
wolves, who traditionally have the right to come and go as they please.

Exits.Description: You can leave the House of Lords.
You see a dais, upon which is a large carved chair.
You see a dais, upon which is a large carved chair.
You see a dais, upon which is a large carved chair.

Rooms.Name: The Seat of Assent
Rooms.Description:
The Seat of Assent is raised upon a dais to the south of this part of 
the House. Those in agreement with the High Seat move to this part of 
the house in order to register their vote. It is the job of the Seat of 
Assent to count those votes. Only the tigers can hold official positions 
in the House of Lords like the High Seat, and the Seats of Assent and 
Rejection.

Exits.Description: The main part of the House of Lords lies to the east.
The High Seat lies to the south.

Rooms.Name: The High Seat
Rooms.Description:
The High Seat is where the final say in the government of Werehome 
rests. While most decisions are democratically made, the Lord who sits 
on the High Seat has the deciding vote. The Lords among the tigers take 
it in turns to sit on the high seat, each one serving for one lunar 
cycle before another takes over.  The seat itself looks pretty 
uncomfortable, but it's clearly supposed to be more symbolic than 
functional.

Exits.Description: The main part of the House of Lords lies to the north.

Rooms.Name: The Seat of Rejection
Rooms.Description:
When the werefolk vote, those in opposition move over to this side of 
the house. On a dais to the south sits a large chair (almost a throne) 
which has an unobstructed view of this side of the house. This is the 
Seat of Rejection. Whichever tiger lord is serving this post at the time 
will count the number of votes against, and relay this information to 
the High Seat.

Exits.Description: The High Seat lies to the south.
The main part of the House of Lords lies to the west.

Rooms.Name: Dark path
Rooms.Description:
The light fades in this direction, until you can barely make out the 
way forward. Very soon the paved walkway gives way to a well trampled 
trail though the undergrowth. You can make out all kinds of different 
footprints, human and animal. The path continues to the east, but the 
light of the entrance shines enticingly from the west.

Exits.Description: The path continues through the darkness.
You can see the well-lit entrance to werehome

Rooms.Name: Twist in the path
Rooms.Description:
The trail continues through the undergrowth, wayward branches and 
limbs have been pushed aside by creatures who pass this way more 
regularly. The path is very dim, the light given off by the rocks 
overhead has the hue and brightness of moonlight.

Exits.Description: You can make out a silver gate to the north.
There is a narrow and dark path leading west.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to the hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
A huge silver gate to the north marks the entrance to the Hunting 
Garden of the werefolk. Here they can practice stalking, and killing. 
You can't see anyone from here, but you can here an occasional scream, 
or rustle of bushes.

Exits.Description: You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
A twisting path leads south.

Rooms.Name: Hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
Leaves rustle somewhere off to your right, and you can hear the low 
rhythmic breathing of some ferocious beast. You hear a piercing shriek in 
the distance, which cuts off abruptly. This doesn't seem like a very safe 
place to wander around. The gates lies to the south.

Exits.Description: You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
A way out! Better take it while you have the chance.

Rooms.Name: Hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
Leaves rustle somewhere off to your right, and you can hear the low 
rhythmic breathing of some ferocious beast. You hear a piercing shriek in 
the distance, which cuts off abruptly. This doesn't seem like a very safe 
place to wander around. A severed limb sticks out from under a bush.

Exits.Description: You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks like it was once an arm, though the hand is missing - it looks 
well chewed.

Rooms.Name: Hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
Leaves rustle somewhere off to your right, and you can hear the low 
rhythmic breathing of some ferocious beast. You hear a piercing shriek in 
the distance, which cuts off abruptly. This doesn't seem like a very safe 
place to wander around. Tracks in the dust indicate a recent struggle.

Exits.Description: You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.

Rooms.Name: Hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
Leaves rustle somewhere off to your right, and you can hear the low 
rhythmic breathing of some ferocious beast. You hear a piercing shriek in 
the distance, which cuts off abruptly. This doesn't seem like a very safe 
place to wander around. You accidentally stand in a pool of blood.

Exits.Description: You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Eeek! Its still warm. Small clawed bloody footprints lead west. You 
think you can hear breathing.

Rooms.Name: Hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
Leaves rustle somewhere off to your right, and you can hear the low 
rhythmic breathing of some ferocious beast. You hear a piercing shriek in 
the distance, which cuts off abruptly. This doesn't seem like a very safe 
place to wander around. A bush off to your left twitches.

Exits.Description: You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.

Rooms.Name: Hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
Leaves rustle somewhere off to your right, and you can hear the low 
rhythmic breathing of some ferocious beast. You hear a piercing shriek in 
the distance, which cuts off abruptly. This doesn't seem like a very safe 
place to wander around. To the north you can see a filthy cage.

Exits.Description: A rusty cage lies to the north.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.

Rooms.Name: Hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
Leaves rustle somewhere off to your right, and you can hear the low 
rhythmic breathing of some ferocious beast. You hear a piercing shriek in 
the distance, which cuts off abruptly. This doesn't seem like a very safe 
place to wander around.

Exits.Description: You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.

Rooms.Name: Hunting garden
Rooms.Description:
Leaves rustle somewhere off to your right, and you can hear the low 
rhythmic breathing of some ferocious beast. You hear a piercing shriek in 
the distance, which cuts off abruptly. This doesn't seem like a very safe 
place to wander around.

Exits.Description: You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.
You can barely see anything in the gloom of the hunting garden.

Rooms.Name: Cage
Rooms.Description:
This filthy cage must be where victims are kept before being 
released into the hunting gardens. The bars are rusty, and the floor is 
covered with grubby straw. There is evidence that both humans and 
animals have been kept here, and the smell is very unpleasant. The cage 
extends further to the east.

Exits.Description: The filthy cage extends to the east.
The eerie silence of the hunting garden lies to the south.

Rooms.Name: Cage
Rooms.Description:
The cage is even most disgusting at this end, the inhabitants have 
tended to huddle here in order to avoid being released into the 
hunting garden. The floor is filthy, and you can see blood stains, 
probably the result of squabbling between prisoners. In the far corner is 
a depression in the floor, where one of the unlucky inhabitants of the 
cage has previously tried to tunnel out.

Exits.Description: The cage continues to the west.

Rooms.Name: Beginning of the Cat Quarter
Rooms.Description:
A narrow tunnel leads into the home of the werecats, so narrow in 
fact that you are forced to crawl and twist and turn in order to 
continue. The lithe catfolk however obviously don't have the same 
problems, else they would surely have done something about it.

Exits.Description:
The twisting tunnel continues, but you can see that it opens out to 
the east.
The safety of the main street is to the west.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to the Terraced Garden
Rooms.Description:
An amazing sight greets your eyes, as you leave the narrow passageway 
you stand before a beautiful indoor garden, with flowers and bushes 
hiding all the ground, and walls, apart from a few narrow winding 
pathways. The garden is terraced, with alcoves on both main levels, 
where the werecats obviously sleep. Of all the werefolk the werecats 
are most like their totem, and often spend months at a time in their 
animal form.

Exits.Description: You can continue into the beautiful flower garden.
A narrow twisting tunnel leads west.

Rooms.Name: Lower Terrace
Rooms.Description:
The smell of flowers is so intoxicating it makes your head swim. All 
around you are small niches where you can make out the sleeping forms of 
cats. It's warm and humid in here too, much warmer than other parts of 
the city, but the plants seem to flourish in the heat. This terrace 
extends further to the north, or there is another tiny path leading 
upwards to the next terrace.

Exits.Description: A twisting pathway heads north.
You can see the entrance to the garden.
A narrow well-kept walkway leads to the upper terrace.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Not your average house trained cats, these are real mean 
looking wildcats!

Rooms.Name: Lower Terrace
Rooms.Description:
The heady perfume of the terraced garden is even stronger at this 
end. Of course, there is no breeze to disperse the scent, which is 
beginning to give you a headache. A twisting path leads up to the next 
level of the gardens, its not an easy path for you, but it is for the 
agile werecats.

Exits.Description: A twisting pathway heads south.
A narrow gravel walkway leads to the upper terrace.

Rooms.Name: Upper Terrace
Rooms.Description:
The gardens are immaculately kept, all the plants are well trimmed, 
and dead flower heads have been removed. The narrow pathways are also 
beautifully cared for, the werecats are obviously very meticulous about 
their homes.

Exits.Description: A winding pathway goes south.
You can head down to the lower terrace.

Rooms.Name: Upper Terrace
Rooms.Description:
You almost lose your balance several times as you wander along the 
narrow pathways. The fragrant terrace garden extends further to the 
north, or there is a twisting walkway leading down to the lower terrace.
The foliage to the east looks a little thinner than elsewhere.

Exits.Description: A twisting pathway leads north.
If you are agile you can scramble through the foliage to the east.
You can head down to the lower terrace.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: An agile person might make it through here.

Rooms.Name: Wolf Run
Rooms.Description:
This tunnel leads to the home of the wolves, the most powerful sect 
of the werefolk. They are known to be aggressive, and merciless to any 
who invade their caverns, so you'd better watch out! The walls are 
carved with what appears to be writing, though you can't be certain.

Exits.Description: You can see the House of Lords to the west.
A tunnel leads down into the darkness.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It appears to be a history of the werewolves, from their earliest 
memories, before they came to werehome, to the present day. There are 
many drawings of werewolf heroes, and sacred symbols to preserve their 
memory.

Rooms.Name: Twisting Caves
Rooms.Description:
The caves of the wolves are incredibly complex, with winding tunnels 
leading in all directions, but quickly twisting out of sight. At a 
glance it look far less prosperous than the homes of the tigers, but a 
closer look reveals that gems and precious metals are to be found 
everywhere, and everything is beautifully crafted.

Exits.Description: Twisting tunnels start off leading north, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading east, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading south, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading west, but quickly change direction.
A twisting tunnel leads upwards.

Rooms.Name: Twisting Caves
Rooms.Description:
The caves of the wolves are incredibly complex, with winding tunnels 
leading in all directions, but quickly twisting out of sight. At a 
glance it look far less prosperous than the homes of the tigers, but a 
closer look reveals that gems and precious metals are to be found 
everywhere, and everything is beautifully crafted.

Exits.Description: Twisting tunnels start off leading north, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading east, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading south, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading west, but quickly change direction.
A twisting tunnel leads upwards.

Rooms.Description:
The caves of the wolves are incredibly complex, with winding tunnels 
leading in all directions, but quickly twisting out of sight. At a 
glance it look far less prosperous than the homes of the tigers, but a 
closer look reveals that gems and precious metals are to be found 
everywhere, and everything is beautifully crafted.

Exits.Description: Twisting tunnels start off leading north, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading east, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading south, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading west, but quickly change direction.
A twisting tunnel leads upwards.

Rooms.Description:
The caves of the wolves are incredibly complex, with winding tunnels

glance it look far less prosperous than the homes of the tigers, but a

Exits.Description: Twisting tunnels start off leading north, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading east, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading south, but quickly change direction.
Twisting tunnels start off leading west, but quickly change direction.
A twisting tunnel leads upwards.

Rooms.Name: Entrance to the Boar quarter
Rooms.Description:
The boar quarter is like its inhabitants - well built, but rather 
simple. While the boars are powerful fighters, they do not compare to 
the wolves, so they try to be more like the civilised tigers. The home 
of the wereboars lies to the east, and the main street to the west.

Exits.Description: You can make out a particularly hideous fountain to the east.
Main street lies to the west.

Rooms.Name: Boar shaped fountain
Rooms.Description:
The centre of the Boar quarter is dominated by a large fountain of a 
wereboar. The homes of the wereboars appear to be a series of recessed 
caverns which form an arc about the fountain. You could investigate the 
homes to the north, east and south, or you could leave west.

Exits.Description: The homes of the boars start to the north, curving round to the east.
You can see the homes of the boars, curving round to the north and south.
The homes of the boars start to the south, curving round to the east.
You can leave the boar-quarter to the west.

Rooms.Name: Boar House
Rooms.Description:
Unlike the elegant homes of the weretigers, those of the boars seem 
a bit gaudy. Any attempt on their part to appear cultured seems instead 
to make them look a bit silly. You wonder how anyone could take the 
boars seriously, but then you remember how large and powerful they are.

Exits.Description: The homes of the boars continue to the east.
You can see a particularly hideous fountain to the south.

Rooms.Name: Boar House
Rooms.Description:
Unlike the elegant homes of the weretigers, those of the boars seem 
a bit gaudy. Any attempt on their part to appear cultured seems instead 
to make them look a bit silly. You wonder how anyone could take the 
boars seriously, but then you remember how large and powerful they are.

Exits.Description: The homes of the boars continue to the north.
The homes of the boars continue to the south.
You can see a particularly hideous fountain to the west.
Steps lead downwards.

Rooms.Name: Boar House
Rooms.Description:
Unlike the elegant homes of the weretigers, those of the boars seem 
a bit gaudy. Any attempt on their part to appear cultured seems instead 
to make them look a bit silly. You wonder how anyone could take the 
boars seriously, but then you remember how large and powerful they are.

Exits.Description: You can see a particularly hideous fountain to the north.
The homes of the boars continue to the east.

Rooms.Name: Sanctum of the Tiger
Rooms.Description:
The hidden sanctuary below the statue is a little surprising, 
considering the tigers' tendancy towards ostentation. This, however, is 
their most sacred place. Only the High Priest, and his acolytes are 
allowed in here normally, and on special occasions the Lords among the 
weretigers are also permitted to gather here.

Exits.Description: There is a trapdoor in the ceiling.

Rooms.Name: Sanctum of the wolf
Rooms.Description:
The devotion of the wolves is legendary, and the inner sanctum of 
their temple is an amazing shrine, not just to their totem, but also to 
their ancestors, from whom they believe their power partly comes. The 
walls are lined with miniature statues of werewolf heroes and plundered 
treasures. The centre of the room is inlaid with a huge wolfs' head, in 
gold - and represents more wealth than everything else in the city 
together.

Exits.Description: A black door, carved with a wolfshead leads north.

Rooms.Name: Main Street
Rooms.Description:
You stand in the middle of the main street through Werehome. The 
entrance to the city is to the north, and the street continues to the 
south. To the east you can see a narrow pathway, which becomes narrower 
as is twists out of view. The street is lit as bright as day by the 
strange phosphorescent rocks that line the cave high above your head.

Exits.Description: You can see the entrance to Werehome to the north.
A narrow tunnel leads east.
The main street continues to the south.

Rooms.Name: Lord Birt's Chambers
Rooms.Description:
Talk about slumming it! This place is a real mess, bits of trash 
everywhere. The wererats are notorious scavengers, and it seems that 
Lord Birt gets the lion's share. How anyone stands the smell you'll 
never know. Better not let anyone catch you rummaging in here.

Exits.Description: You can climb back out of the junk pile.

Rooms.Name: Twisting Caves
Rooms.Description:
These particular caves are the home of one of werehome's more famous 
inhabitants, the werewolf Lord Xamon. The walls are lined with gold, and 
gems, and precious souvenirs of his travels. The room is brightly lit 
by a huge chandelier made from a dragons skull. (You would be right to 
assume that Xamon killed the dragon himself)

Exits.Description: A twisting tunnel leads downwards.

Rooms.Name: Kralian's Chambers
Rooms.Description:
This comfortable alcove is the home of the leader of the werecats, 
Lord Kralian. There has never been a more graceful and cunning werecat 
in the history of werehome. The walls are lined with flowers, and vines, 
and the floor is carpeted with lush foliage.

Exits.Description: If you are agile, you can fit through a gap in the foliage.

Rooms.Name: Lord Dorlan's chamber
Rooms.Description:
Simple furnishings, for a simple Lord. Its all very homely, with a 
comfy chair and pictures on the wall. And a huge number of skulls in one 
corner. He may prefer to eat out - but obviously he gets food delivered 
fairly often too.

Exits.Description: Steps lead upwards.

Mobs.Name: werewolf wolf were
Mobs.LongDescription: A powerful werewolf strides purposefully down the street.
Mobs.Description:
Humanoid in shape, but with facial features resembling those of a 
wolf, the werewolf is obviously very strong and quick. He walks around 
with an air of superiority, master of all he surveys.

Mobs.Name: wereboar boar were
Mobs.LongDescription: A wereboar struts about self-importantly.
Mobs.Description:
The wereboar is very heavily built, with wide shoulders and arms roped 
with thick muscle. He doesnt look particularly intelligent, but then its 
likely he prefers violence to chess.

Mobs.Name: werecat cat were
Mobs.LongDescription: A werecat picks his way nimbly across the street.
Mobs.Description:
At a first glance he looks like a human, but a closer look shows that 
the short hair on his head is really fur, and his eyes are slitted. He 
moves very gracefully, almost gliding across the street. Occasionally he 
clicks his claws together - a kind of nervous twitch.

Mobs.Name: wererat rat were
Mobs.LongDescription: A devious wererat skulks around here.
Mobs.Description:
With his beady eyes and twitchy nose, this humanoid creature resembles a
rat. Glancing suspiciously around he dry-washes his hands nervously. He 
certainly looks an untrustworthy individual - I'd check my pockets if I 
were you.

Mobs.Name: weretiger tiger were
Mobs.LongDescription: A mighty weretiger stalks confidently down the street.
Mobs.Description:
He looks born to rule, with a calm penetrating gaze, and a powerful
build. He is well dressed, and moves confidently, his eyes scanning the
whole street. His eyes are slitted, and a very pale yellow, his hair is
a light reddish colour, with darker stripes.

Mobs.Name: werewolf wolf were
Mobs.LongDescription: A powerful werewolf snarls at you.
Mobs.Description:
Can you believe it? You travel all this way to take a look round his 
home and he's not pleased to see you? Some people have no manners. It'd 
probably be best to go now, before he starts some trouble.

Mobs.Name: wereboar boar were
Mobs.LongDescription: A wereboar mumbles unitelligibly at you.
Mobs.Description:
He's certainly well built, but you can tell that he's not exactly the 
sharpest tool in the box. He looks at you suspicously, and looking into 
his eyes you can tell that he's trying to figure out why you don't look 
like the other wereboars. You better leave before he figures it out.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote looks blankly at you.;
%10 mumbles to himself.

Mobs.Name: werecat cat were
Mobs.LongDescription: A werecat blinks as he looks at you.
Mobs.Description:
He blinks at you, and rubs his eyes as if he has just awakened. You 
better not have disturbed him! Like a domestic cat he likes to sleep, 
but unlike a his domesticated cousins, he is likely to rip your arms 
off if you've upset him.

Mobs.Name: wererat rat were
Mobs.LongDescription: A sneaky wererat regards you suspiciously from across the street.
Mobs.Description:
He's a devious fellow, theres no doubt, I'd keep an eye on my gold if I 
were you. His beady little eyes size you up, weighing and measuring, I 
bet he could tell you your entire inventory.

Mobs.Name: weretiger tiger were
Mobs.LongDescription: A proud weretiger surveys the room.
Mobs.Description:
He stands head and shoulders above everone else, gazing 
impassively around him. His calm face gives away his 
confidence at being able to handle anything life throws 
at him.

Mobs.Name: weretiger priest high were tiger
Mobs.ShortDescription: the High Priest of the weretigers
Mobs.LongDescription: The High Priest of the weretigers is here, mumbling canticles.
Mobs.Description:
He's dressed in long white flowing robes, with a purple trim. He's 
obviously deeply religious, he murmurs his prayers to his totem, the 
tiger, almost constantly.

Mobs.Name: werewolf shaman were wolf
Mobs.LongDescription: The Shaman of the Werewolves is chanting here.
Mobs.Description:
Unlike his kinsfolk, who are a bizarre mixture of wolf and man, the 
Shaman has a wolf's head and a mans body. His shapeshifting skills have 
been honed by his meditations to such a degree that he can metamorphose 
different parts of himself, almost at will. He wears a ragged collection 
of robes and amulets, and carries a small rod with a golden wolfshead.

Mobs.Name: wererat priest rat were
Mobs.LongDescription: The Priest of the Wererats is checking the collection plate.
Mobs.Description:
He doesn't look very reputable, but then neither do the rest of the 
wererats. He keeps looking in the collection plate, and you cant help 
noticing that he occasionally removes some of the coins and places 
them in his own pocket.

Mobs.Name: werecat priest cat were
Mobs.LongDescription: The Priest of the Werecats is watching over his people.
Mobs.Description:
With his slightly pointed ears, and short hair, he looks very handsome. 
His slitted yellow eyes glance at you as you enter, and watch you as you 
move around. Clearly he doesnt trust you around his flock.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote watches you suspiciously.;
%10 emote glances around the room.

Mobs.Name: wereboar priest boar were
Mobs.ShortDescription: the High Priest of the wereboars
Mobs.LongDescription: The High Priest of the wereboars is trying to count his congregation.
Mobs.Description:
Dressed in long flowing robes, he looks fairly respectable, but as he 
surveys his temple, you get the impression that he's trying (in vain) to 
count the people there.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote looks puzzled.;
%10 emote grunts something at you.

Mobs.Name: korgan huntsmaster wolf were werewolf
Mobs.LongDescription: The Huntsmaster of the werefolk suddenly appears from behind you.
Mobs.Description:
Korgan is the hero that all the werefolk (not just the wolves) wish to 
emulate. He truly is a magnificent sight as he towers over you. His arms 
are banded with thick muscle, and his fur is tinged silver-grey. His 
teeth are as large as your fingers, and his eyes glow with power.

Mobs.Name: werewolf hunting were wolf
Mobs.LongDescription: A werewolf is hunting here.
Mobs.Description:
Metamorphosed into lupine form, the werewolf looks like a powerful 
timber wolf. Standing as high as your waist, his hackles rise as he 
looks at you. He bares his teeth in warning, and a low growl begins 
in his throat, I think he just found his lunch - You!
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote growls at you.;
%95 hide

Mobs.Name: weretiger hunting were tiger
Mobs.LongDescription: A weretiger is here, looking for a snack.
Mobs.Description:
It's a bit late for eating out - but the hunting garden is always open, 
and thanks to the hard work of Huntsmaster Korgan, well stocked.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote growls at you.;
%95 hide

Mobs.Name: wererat hunting were rat
Mobs.LongDescription: A wererat tries to sneak up on you.
Mobs.Description:
His sharp little teeth glint in the dim light of the hunting garden, and 
he stares at you with piercing black eyes. He's too small to eat you 
whole, but that doesn't mean he won't try to eat bits of you!
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote looks at you and licks his lips.;
%95 hide

Mobs.Name: werecat hunting were cat
Mobs.LongDescription: A werecat stalks carefully through the bushes.
Mobs.Description:
He's incredibly graceful, as he moves towards you through the 
undergrowth. Hmm...wait a second, while you admiring his style - he's 
got his eye on your leg, and he looks very hungry.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote growls.;
%95 hide

Mobs.Name: wereboar hunting were boar
Mobs.LongDescription: A wereboar munches happily on a severed limb.
Mobs.Description:
He's very heavily built, this wereboar, and so clearly needs alot of 
food to keep him going. He may be a bit 'thinking impaired' but he seems 
to have dismembered his lunch very efficiently.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote burps.;
%95 hide

Mobs.Name: weretiger were tiger high seat
Mobs.LongDescription: The High Seat leads the werefolk.
Mobs.Description:
Each of the weretigers take it in turns to take up the office of High 
Seat. Each lasts for a single month, after which another takes his 
place. Being the leader of all the werefolk is a heavy burden, and the 
strain shows in his dulled eyes, and slumping shoulders. Still, he seems 
proud to serve.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote looks very tired.;
%10 emote peers wearily around the House.

Mobs.Name: weretiger were tiger seat assent
Mobs.LongDescription: The Seat of Assent is counting votes.
Mobs.Description:
The Seat of Assent is an official post, which is rotated through the 
were tigers on a monthly basis. His job is to count the votes in favour 
of any motion put before the Werehome House of Lords.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote peers around the House.;
%10 emote carefully re-checks his counting.

Mobs.Name: weretiger were tiger seat rejection
Mobs.LongDescription: The Seat of Rejection is counting votes.
Mobs.Description:
Every month a different weretiger holds the post of Seat of Rejection. 
When a motion is put before the House of Lords, he counts to number of 
votes against, and relays this information to the High Seat.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote stands on the tips of his toes, to get a better view.;
%10 emote carefully counts the votes.

Mobs.Name: birt wererat lord were rat
Mobs.LongDescription: The Lord of the wererats is gloating over his collection of junk.
Mobs.Description:
Lord Birt is the sneakiest, most lightfingered, and most devious of all 
the wererats. No wonder then, that he is also their leader and most 
admired hero. While you look at him he stares back, he's already made 
a note of everything in your inventory, and is probably about to help 
himself to it.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote tries to slip his hand into your pocket.;
%10 emote rubs his hands together with glee.

Mobs.Name: dorlan wereboar lord were boar
Mobs.LongDescription: Lord Dorlan is struggling with some paperwork.
Mobs.Description:
He's not the sharpest tool in the box (if you know what I mean) but 
sadly for the wereboars, he's the sharpest tool in their box. However, 
you would be wise not to underestimate him. He's very heavily built, 
with a jutting pugnacious jaw, and fists like cured hams.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote growls.;
%10 emote glares at you.

Mobs.Name: kralian werecat lord were cat
Mobs.LongDescription: Lord Kralian looks after all his people.
Mobs.Description:
The werecats were the last of the werefolk to arrive at werehome, and 
though is was a long time ago by human standards, the long-lived 
werecats remember Lord Kralian's role in bringing them to their home. 
Old he might be, but he moves with the agility of a cat, and his 
reactions are like lightning.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote yawns.;
%10 emote flexes his muscles.

Mobs.Name: xamon werewolf lord were wolf
Mobs.LongDescription: The mightiest of all the werefolk towers over you.
Mobs.Description:
Lord Xamon is the largest werewolf you have ever seen, you barely stand 
as high as his chest. His deeds outstrip even those of Huntsmaster 
Korgan - it's said he once killed a huge golden dragon with his bare 
hands. The same hands that are poised to rip out your throat.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%10 emote ROARS!

Mobs.Name: loremaster weretiger were tiger
Mobs.LongDescription: An ancient weretiger waits to pass on his wisdom.
Mobs.Description:
Once a proud weretiger, the loremaster has done it all, seen the outside 
and fought dragons and demons, and spent years studying the ancient lore 
of the werefolk. You can feel his wisdom as you look into his eyes, 
and a sense of calm descends upon you.

Mobs.Name: aaron shopkeeper expedition werewolf were wolf
Mobs.LongDescription:
A burly werewolf will sell you everything you could need for an 
expedition.
Mobs.Description:
He's pretty well built, and has quite a few scars, showing that he knows 
what he's talking about when he tries to sell you adventuring equipment.

Mobs.Name: prisoner filthy human
Mobs.LongDescription: A ragged and filthy prisoner cowers before you.
Mobs.Description:
He's not been well looked after, his eyes are wide with terror and lack 
of food has turned him into a shadow of a human being. He's covered in 
his own filth as he cringes on the ground in front of you, begging for 
his life.

Mobs.Name: prisoner bloody elven elf
Mobs.LongDescription: A ragged elf looks beaten and bruised.
Mobs.Description:
He looks like he's been put through a mill, his arms are covered with 
weeping sores and his clothes are dirty and torn.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote cowers before you.;
%10 emote weeps piteously.

Mobs.Name: prisoner dwarven dwarf
Mobs.LongDescription: A dwarf tries in vain to hide under a bush.
Mobs.Description:
His eyes are dull, and is beard is patchy and matted with blood and 
filth. He has a hunted look, and constantly scans the area, as he 
scrabbles at the ground, trying to hide.
Mobs.ActionScript:
%%10 emote scrabbles at the ground, making his fingers bleed.;
%10 emote cringes in fear.

Objects.Name: plate collection
Objects.Description: A collection plate stands near the entrance to the temple.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Hmm...not much in it, perhaps someone has been helping themslves to the 
contents.

Objects.Name: coins few tarnished copper
Objects.Description: A pitiful number of tarnished coins lie by your feet.

Objects.Name: talisman wolf
Objects.Description: A talisman shaped like the head of a wolf glitters on the ground.

Objects.Name: talisman rat
Objects.Description: A talisman shaped like the head of a rat glitters on the ground.

Objects.Name: talisman cat
Objects.Description: A talisman shaped like the head of a cat glitters on the ground.

Objects.Name: talisman tiger
Objects.Description: A talisman shaped like the head of a tiger glitters on the ground.

Objects.Name: talisman boar
Objects.Description: A talisman shaped like the head of a boar glitters on the ground.

Objects.Name: talisman silver
Objects.Description: A silver talisman in the shape of a wolf fang glitters on the ground.

Objects.Name: fountain marble
Objects.Description:
A white marble fountain, flecked with red and blue, stands in the centre
of the square.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It's rather splendid, constructed entirely out of curves, with no 
angular corners, and the smooth coloured marble is very pleasing 
to the eye.

Objects.Name: fountain boar shaped
Objects.Description: a hideous boar-shaped fountain catches your eye.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It truly does look awful! A feeble attempt at a proud boar 
unrinates sour tasting water into a wide bowl.

Objects.Name: flowers beautiful bunch
Objects.Description: You're sure noone would mind if you picked a few flowers.

Objects.Name: claws ripper
Objects.Description: A razor sharp set of claws are embedded in the ground.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Worn like a set of knuckle dusters, these claws are about a foot long, 
and are so finely sharpened that they disappear when turned edge on.

Objects.Name: werelords werelord signet ring moon
Objects.Description: A signet ring glows like the moon.

Objects.Name: collar shimmering kralian
Objects.Description: A shimmering collar, with an ivory crescent, twinkles in the corner.

Objects.Name: mantle red
Objects.Description: A rich red mantle lined with silver fur looks very warm.

Objects.Name: leather rat mask
Objects.Description: You notice a black leather mask, moulded into the shape of a rat's head.

Objects.Name: rations travel
Objects.Description: Some nutritious travel rations have been left behind.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Nutritious *and* delicious - what more could you ask?

Objects.Name: scroll leaping look before leap
Objects.Description: A scroll jumps and twitches on the ground. (leaping)

Objects.Name: scroll travelling
Objects.Description: A scroll looks ready to leave without you.

Objects.Name: staff lore
Objects.Description: A carved staff with silver caps stands in the corner.

Objects.Name: sceptre golden wolfshead
Objects.Description: You notice a sceptre, topped with a golden wolfshead.

Objects.Name: robes priests
Objects.Description: White robes, with purple trim, obviously belong to a priest.
